newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Speed of NZD rise more a problem than value - Peters.
newsitem.headline: Speed of NZD rise more a problem than value - Peters.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters said on Wednesday the currency's rate of appreciation was more problematic than its high value.
He acknowledged in a speech to a business lunch in Tauranga that there were concerns in some quarters about the high Kiwi dollar, particularly its impact on exporters.
"It is not the value that is so much the problem, but the speed with which the dollar has moved," Peters said.
"You should take heart from a Reserve Bank statement a week ago that the upward movement may have peaked, that the velocity has been arrested."

Peters said the government was doing something constructive to help exporters, by running healthy budget surpluses for the next three years, reducing the costs of government on an ongoing basis, and directing government expenditure only to where it was effective and most needed.
"By minimising inflationary pressure, lead government assists not only exporters, but all producers of wealth in New Zealand," Peters said.
